correctness.rationale: Gaussian-prime splitting, the Euler product, and the interval-filling lemma prove the exact theorem. Seven exact finite rational tail inequalities, 66 certified split-prime anchors covering norms 29 to 8e9, and the unconditional theta progression theorem establish every tail overlap. Exact ramified factor algebra produces [1,C] and [5/4,Z], which are disjoint because C<5/4.

originality.rationale: Exact Gaussian divisors and dual split-prime norms are absent from inspected ordinary integer range theorems. Defant introduces the Gaussian function without a closure formula, Sanna proves a general integer-range component method, and indexed research records nearest exact two-component examples concern alternating and unitary rather than Gaussian reciprocal-fourth sums. Targeted equivalent, broader coverage, table, and implication comparisons did not reveal a covering result; the possibility of an earlier unindexed derivation remains.
residual_risks: Search absence is not proof of global novelty; earlier unindexed Gaussian norm-divisor range classifications may exist.
A generalization of the ordinary divisor-function range method may be published elsewhere but was not identified in the searched corpus.

value.rationale: Exact number and endpoints of connected components of the range of a named Gaussian divisor function are motivated invariants of imaginary quadratic arithmetic. The new split-prime interval-filling phenomenon sharply contrasts the many gaps known for rational integer divisor sums and supplies a complete, not sampled, classification.
